topic-104-a-2-dept-large-language-model-.evolution: Early representatives investigate code scheduling and structured program evolution. Later work applies language models to repository-level context and semantic training. Recent directions include dynamic contamination-aware benchmarks, selective generation based on expected correctness, and joint code–graph representations for hardware design tasks.
openQuestions: How can benchmark transformations preserve difficulty as well as semantics?
What evidence should a code model use to decide when it cannot safely produce a functionally correct answer?
topic-104-a-2-dept-large-language-model-.overview: This topic studies learning systems that generate, understand, or assess programs. It includes repository context, semantic reasoning, compiler tasks, and hardware-description representations. A representative evaluation framework creates semantically equivalent variations of programming problems to probe whether code models handle reasoning beyond familiar benchmark wording.
topic-104-a-2-dept-large-language-model-.title: Code Models, Program Semantics, and Correctness Evaluation
topic-104-a-2-dept-large-language-model-.whyItMatters: Code that appears plausible can still behave incorrectly, and public benchmarks may overlap with training data. Evaluations grounded in behavior, semantics, and controlled problem variation provide stronger evidence than surface similarity or success on a fixed test collection alone.

topic-105-epsilon-softmax-approximating-.evolution: The representatives range from probability forecasting to neural calibration and sharp uncertainty estimates. Recent work examines sample-dependent temperature scaling and uses uncertainty sets to question whether misclassification really demonstrates successful unlearning. These applications show how confidence evaluation can expose weaknesses hidden by ordinary accuracy metrics.
openQuestions: How stable is calibration under distribution changes?
Which uncertainty evaluations distinguish useful caution from uninformative predictions or superficial changes in model behavior?
topic-105-epsilon-softmax-approximating-.overview: Calibration asks whether a model's stated confidence matches how often its predictions are correct. This topic studies training losses, proper scoring rules, density-based uncertainty, ensembles, and post-training recalibration. A representative study investigates focal loss as a way to improve calibration during training, with temperature scaling providing an additional adjustment afterward.
topic-105-epsilon-softmax-approximating-.title: Confidence Calibration and Predictive Uncertainty
topic-105-epsilon-softmax-approximating-.whyItMatters: Accuracy alone does not tell users when to rely on a prediction. Useful uncertainty must be both reliable and informative, supporting decisions such as abstention, comparison, or further inspection without merely making every prediction vague.

topic-106-a-composite-randomized-increme.evolution: Earlier representatives concern regularized objectives and accelerated stochastic methods. Later work extends variance reduction to nonconvex, composite, and minimax problems. Recent directions include dependent stochastic observations, penalty methods, and Riemannian optimization for dimension reduction, adapting the update rule to the structure of the task.
openQuestions: How can methods adapt to noise and regularity without fragile tuning?
Which theoretical speedups persist when gradient and communication costs are measured together?
topic-106-a-composite-randomized-increme.overview: Many learning objectives combine a smooth loss with nonsmooth penalties, constraints, or geometric structure. This topic develops stochastic optimization methods for those settings, including proximal updates, variance reduction, momentum, and manifold-aware algorithms. A representative analysis establishes convergence to stationary points for nonsmooth nonconvex finite-sum problems using constant-size minibatches.
topic-106-a-composite-randomized-increme.title: Variance-Reduced and Composite Stochastic Optimization
topic-106-a-composite-randomized-increme.whyItMatters: Cheap noisy updates are valuable only if their accumulated error remains controlled. Theory clarifies which assumptions permit faster convergence, what type of solution is guaranteed, and when additional computation for variance reduction or constraints is worthwhile.

topic-107-very-likely-means-uncertain-ho.evolution: The representatives include earlier work on human judgments and distribution shift, followed by studies of deployment expectations and language-model judging. Recent methods combine juries, bias analysis, synthetic feedback, or explicit criteria to assess answers, including settings where external verification sources are unavailable.
openQuestions: How can evaluations predict the mistakes users are most likely to encounter?
What independent checks establish that a model-based judge measures the intended quality rather than shared model biases?
topic-107-very-likely-means-uncertain-ho.overview: Language-model evaluation involves both measuring capability and understanding how people interpret that capability. This cluster examines human generalization from observed successes, model-based judges, judgment bias, and hallucination detection. One representative study models how people infer where a system will perform well after seeing it succeed or fail on other tasks.
topic-107-very-likely-means-uncertain-ho.title: Human Expectations and Language-Model Evaluation
topic-107-very-likely-means-uncertain-ho.whyItMatters: A model can be broadly capable yet unreliable on the tasks people select for it. Automated judges can expand evaluation coverage, but their agreement, validity, and blind spots need examination rather than being assumed from fluent explanations.

topic-108-a-1-000-neuron-system-with-one.evolution: The representatives span bit-serial networks and pulse-stream CMOS chips through circuit-level gradient methods. Recent work studies nonideal references in analog training and agent-assisted circuit sizing. Error-based predictive coding takes a complementary route by reformulating the dynamics for digital efficiency, trading direct analog implementability for faster numerical computation.
openQuestions: Which learning rules remain stable under realistic device variation?
How should comparisons account for simulation overhead, physical precision, and end-to-end training energy?
topic-108-a-1-000-neuron-system-with-one.overview: This topic connects neural computation with circuits and physical dynamical systems. Early papers implement neural operations and gradient-based learning in analog VLSI, where signal representation and circuit behavior shape the algorithm. Later work addresses analog in-memory training, automated circuit design, and the efficiency of digitally simulating physically inspired learning rules.
topic-108-a-1-000-neuron-system-with-one.title: Analog Neural Hardware and Physical Learning Dynamics
topic-108-a-1-000-neuron-system-with-one.whyItMatters: An algorithm's cost depends on the substrate that executes it. Operations natural for analog hardware may be expensive to simulate digitally, while device imperfections can invalidate assumptions made by an idealized learning rule.

topic-109-how-do-language-models-track-s.evolution: Early representatives concern language learning and role binding. Later work examines reasoning and pretrained-transformer behavior. Recent studies combine structural interventions, concept ablation, and grammar-based theory; analyses of subgrammars distinguish learning dynamics and internal alignment from improvements in final predictive performance.
openQuestions: Which mechanistic hypotheses make predictions that distinguish them from alternatives?
How well do findings from controlled grammars explain generalization in natural language and code?
topic-109-how-do-language-models-track-s.overview: This topic investigates what computations language models learn and how those computations transfer beyond familiar examples. Papers study depth, emergent abilities, in-context learning, length generalization, grammar structure, and the reversibility of interventions. One representative analysis deletes or swaps layers and uses differing sensitivity across depth to motivate hypotheses about stages of inference.
topic-109-how-do-language-models-track-s.title: Language-Model Mechanisms and Systematic Generalization
topic-109-how-do-language-models-track-s.whyItMatters: Strong task performance does not uniquely identify the mechanism producing it. Controlled interventions and simplified formal languages can test explanations and reveal why a model generalizes along some dimensions while failing along others.

topic-110-a-comparative-analysis-and-stu.evolution: The representatives move from multiresolution and unsupervised convolutional models to structured convolutions and general attention-based perception. Recent work questions shape sensitivity and adapts pretrained layers for data-limited edge sensing, illustrating continued interest in both representational limits and practical reuse.
openQuestions: Which architectural changes improve shape and compositional understanding under controlled data budgets?
How can transferred layers be selected when source and target sensors have very different statistics?
topic-110-a-comparative-analysis-and-stu.overview: This cluster studies how neural architectures learn useful visual features under constraints on data, parameters, or computation. Topics include convolutions, parameter sharing, layerwise training, attention, and transfer across sensing modalities. A representative architecture ties groups of convolutional filters through translations, seeking stronger representations or lower memory use through additional structure.
topic-110-a-comparative-analysis-and-stu.title: Visual Architecture Design and Efficient Representation Transfer
topic-110-a-comparative-analysis-and-stu.whyItMatters: Architectural assumptions determine which patterns a model learns efficiently and which variations it handles naturally. Comparing accuracy with resource requirements and transfer behavior helps reveal whether a design captures useful structure or mainly benefits from scale.

topic-111-d-2-decentralized-training-ove.evolution: Earlier representatives address distributed value functions and adaptive networks. Later work develops unified analyses for changing topologies and faster gradient tracking. Recent papers examine communication compression, alternative mixing matrices, and certified removal of a participant's influence using information from training trajectories.
openQuestions: How can communication schedules adapt to changing topology and heterogeneous data?
Can stability-based guarantees remain informative at the scale and nonconvexity of modern collaborative training?
topic-111-d-2-decentralized-training-ove.overview: Decentralized learning lets connected workers optimize collaboratively without routing every update through a central coordinator. This topic studies local updates, network mixing, gradient tracking, minimax objectives, and compressed communication. A representative analysis uses algorithmic stability to examine how communication topology affects generalization as well as convergence.
topic-111-d-2-decentralized-training-ove.title: Decentralized Optimization, Communication, and Stability
topic-111-d-2-decentralized-training-ove.whyItMatters: Reducing communication can save time, but disagreement between workers introduces additional error. Useful guarantees must account for data differences, graph connectivity, and the interaction between local computation and information exchange.
